name: Protein_MSA_inspect
description: Inspect local single-component protein A3M or aligned FASTA. Reports raw/unique depth, query-only or duplicate-only inputs, query match, gaps and insertions. No uploads, homology search, Neff or folding validation. Inspect each complex component separately.

alignment_path.description: Local single-component protein A3M or aligned FASTA path; stays local. Exactly one input source.

alignment_content.description: Inline single-component protein A3M or aligned FASTA; stays local. Exactly one input source.

format.description: Default a3m: lowercase residues and dots are insertions. aligned_fasta normalizes lowercase and treats dots as gaps.

expected_query_sequence.description: Optional expected ungapped protein sequence, compared to first record. Mismatch is reported; no sequences returned.

max_row_details.description: Bound per-row summaries; default 10. Counts stay complete.

all_gap_row_count.description: Rows that are nothing but gaps. They inflate the depth without adding evidence.

duplicate_aligned_row_count.description: Rows whose aligned sequence repeats another's. Duplicates inflate apparent depth, which is what coverage-based confidence is computed from.

format.description: Alignment format detected, e.g. 'a3m', 'fasta', 'stockholm'. a3m encodes insertions as lower case, so a reader that ignores the format miscounts columns.

insertion_gap_count.description: Gap characters inside those insertion columns.

insertion_residue_count.description: Residues in insertion columns - the lower-case positions a3m uses, which are not part of the query's coordinate frame.

limitations.description: What the measurement itself does not account for, e.g. 'First record is treated as query; identity includes gaps as nonmatches'. 4 on the measured call. Without them the identity figure reads as more authoritative than it is.

mean_query_site_coverage.description: Mean fraction of rows covering each query position, e.g. 1.0. The usual proxy for how much evidence each position has.

mean_query_site_identity.description: Mean identity to the query across its positions, e.g. 1.0.

nonempty_nonquery_row_count.description: How many rows other than the query carry any aligned residue. 0 means the alignment is query-only and carries no homologue information at all, however many rows it has.

query_gap_count.description: Gap characters in the query row.

query_residue_count.description: Residues in the query (first) record, e.g. 4.

row_details.description: Per-row figures: row_index, aligned_residue_count, query_site_coverage and identity. Where a single bad row can be found.

row_details_truncated.description: True when row_details holds fewer rows than the alignment has, so the per-row view is a sample.

source_kind.description: Where the alignment came from, e.g. 'alignment_content' (supplied inline) or a file path. What was actually inspected.

warnings.description: What is wrong with this alignment, e.g. 'Query-only alignment: no additional aligned sequence rows.' 2 on the measured call. The numbers above look healthy on a query-only alignment; these sentences are what say it is useless.
